voiceover:
[conversational] Before you pay for Google storage, try this Gmail cleanup first.

Gmail, Drive and Photos share one storage pool.

On a computer, open Gmail and type this in the search bar: has:attachment larger:10M. Press Enter.

Tick the Select checkbox. [whispers] Here's the step most people miss: that only picks the 50 on screen. Click "Select all conversations that match this search", then hit the trash icon.

Repeat with category:promotions older_than:2y. Then older_than:2y larger:10M. Then has:attachment older_than:2y.

[serious] Now the catch: deleted mail still counts. Go to More, Trash, "Empty Trash now". Then More, Spam, "Delete all spam messages now."

It's permanent, so add -is:starred and skim for receipts first. The phone app can't select all, and Drive or Photos might be the real hog. Check one.google.com/storage.

[curious] What's eating most of your storage, Gmail, Drive or Photos?

Send this to the friend whose Gmail says storage is almost full.
title: BEFORE YOU PAY GOOGLE

research.tool: Gmail search operators (larger:, has:attachment, category:, older_than:) plus Gmail's "Select all conversations that match this search", Trash and Spam
research.availability: Free. Works in every Gmail account. The full select-all and bulk-delete flow works on Gmail web (desktop, or a mobile browser in desktop mode). The Gmail mobile app accepts the search operators but has no "select all conversations that match this search" option, so you must tap messages one by one.
steps: Click the search bar at the top and type the first query, for example: has:attachment larger:10M. Press Enter.
Tick the Select checkbox at the top-left above the message list. This selects only the 50 conversations on the current page.
Click the banner link "Select all conversations that match this search" (reads like "Select all 2,000 conversations...").
Review the results first, e.g. add -is:starred to protect starred mail. Then click the Delete (trash can) icon at the top and confirm the bulk-action prompt if one appears.
Repeat with the other searches: category:promotions older_than:2y, then older_than:2y larger:10M has:attachment (or older_than:2y has:attachment larger:5M).
In the left sidebar click More, then Trash. Click "Empty Trash now" at the top (or Delete forever), and confirm.
In the left sidebar click More, then Spam. Click "Delete all spam messages now" at the top.
Check the result at one.google.com/storage, which shows the Gmail / Drive / Photos breakdown.
facts: Gmail Help: when you delete a message it moves to Trash, and after 30 days it is deleted permanently.
Google One Help: Gmail messages and attachments, including Spam and Trash, count towards your storage quota. So deleting alone does not free space until you empty Trash and Spam.
Google's Gmail Help desktop steps: More > Trash > "Empty Trash now" / "Delete forever"; More > Spam > "Delete all spam messages now" (or select emails and click "Delete forever").

larger:10M finds emails bigger than 10 MB, including attachments (Mailmeteor 2026 guide). Combining with has:attachment is a common pattern, e.g. has:attachment larger:10M or older_than:2y larger:10M has:attachment.

older_than: accepts d, m and y units (days, months, years). Hours and weeks are not documented (EmailAnalytics, checked against Google's Help page; Google's Refine searches in Gmail page still listed the operators as of Sept 2026).
category:promotions is a valid search, e.g. category:promotions older_than:1y (Superhuman, Carly guides). Gmail has no built-in sort-by-size, so larger: is the workaround (MailSweeper).

The select-all checkbox picks only the current page (50 conversations on web). A banner then offers to select every conversation that matches the search (Google Workspace KB shows the example "All 50 conversations on this page are selected. Select all 2,000 conversations in Inbox.").
Spam is auto-deleted after 30 days, and Trash after 30 days (Mailmeteor, 2sync).
Storage pricing, US (Google One plans page, as of Oct 2026): Basic 100 GB $1.99/mo; Google AI Plus 2 TB $9.99/mo; Google AI Pro 5 TB $19.99/mo. Storage is shared across Photos, Drive and Gmail.

Free storage: Google's official wording is now "up to 15 GB". 9to5Google (May 14, 2026) reports new accounts get 5 GB until a phone number is linked, which unlocks 15 GB. PCWorld says existing accounts are unaffected. Google told Engadget it is a "test" in select regions (via Gizchina).
Gmail storage is shared with Drive and Photos, so freeing Gmail space helps the whole account quota (Google One Help).
If storage stays over quota, Google says you can't upload to Drive or back up Photos, sending and receiving email can be affected, and content may eventually be removed (Google One Help).
do_not_claim: "Delete 5GB in 2 minutes" is unverifiable. Results depend on the mailbox, and many accounts have far less than 5 GB of mail junk. Use "can free up gigabytes" or "depends on your inbox" instead.
"Stop paying for Google storage" or "never pay again" is an overstatement. Heavy Photos or Drive use may still need a paid plan, and Gmail may not be the main storage hog.
"Hidden" or "secret" Gmail codes: the operators are documented in Google's own Help Center (Refine searches in Gmail).
Don't say deleting frees space instantly. Trash and Spam still count towards the quota until emptied, or for 30 days.
Don't say "everyone has 15 GB free". Google now says "up to 15 GB", and new accounts without a phone number may get 5 GB.
Don't say it works the same on phone. Select-all-matching is web only.
Don't claim a single search deletes everything. Each query needs its own select-all and delete.
The caption's "comment STORAGE for a DM" is a lead-gen hook, not a Gmail feature. Don't copy it.
Don't claim larger:10M finds only attachments. It matches total message size. Add has:attachment for attachments.
Don't say Spam goes to Trash first. "Delete all spam messages now" is permanent and immediate (Viral Marketing Lab, secondary source).
criticism: Bulk deletion is hard to undo: after Trash is emptied (or 30 days pass) the mail is gone for good. Back up important mail with Google Takeout first (MailSweeper).

Broad searches like category:promotions or older_than:2y can catch receipts, tickets, tax documents, or 2FA and recovery emails. Review the results, and use -is:starred or -label: to protect important mail.
Search operators don't touch Google Drive or Google Photos, which are often the real storage hogs. Check one.google.com/storage first.
Free storage is shrinking for new accounts: 5 GB without phone verification (9to5Google, PCWorld). Phone number linking is the trade-off for 15 GB.
The Gmail mobile app can't select all matching conversations, so phone users can't bulk-delete this way.

ui.platforms: Gmail web (desktop browser) is the primary platform. The Gmail iOS and Android apps take the search operators but have no select-all-matching option. Storage check on one.google.com or Google Account > Storage.
apps: Google One storage page (one.google.com/storage) for the before/after storage check
screens: Gmail web inbox: search bar across the top centre. Tune/slider icon at the right end of the search box opens the Advanced search panel (Size, Has attachment, Date within, etc.). Left sidebar: Compose, Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Sent, Drafts, then More (expands to Important, Chat, Scheduled, All Mail, Spam, Trash, Categories, Manage labels, Create new label). Inbox tabs sit above the message list: Primary, Promotions, Social, Updates (if enabled). Default theme is light.
Type the query (e.g. has:attachment larger:10M) in the search bar, press Enter. The list shows only matching mail, with the query shown in the search box.
Above the message list, top-left, the Select checkbox. Ticking it shows a banner: "All 50 conversations on this page are selected." with a link "Select all [N] conversations that match this search".

Toolbar above the list shows Archive, Report spam, Delete (trash can), Mark as unread, Snooze, Move to, Labels, More. Click the trash can. A confirmation dialog for the bulk action may appear ("Confirm bulk action" / OK).
Sidebar: More > Trash. Banner at top of the list: "Empty Trash now", with a "Delete forever" button in the toolbar when emails are selected. A confirmation dialog appears; click OK.
Sidebar: More > Spam. Banner at top: "Delete all spam messages now". Click it and confirm.
Optional result screen: one.google.com/storage shows the total used, with a Gmail, Drive and Photos breakdown, and a "Manage storage" or cleanup tool.

research.visuals: A real screen recording of Gmail web is best: the typed query in the search bar, the filtered list, the Select checkbox and the "Select all conversations that match this search" banner, the trash icon, then More > Trash > "Empty Trash now" and More > Spam > "Delete all spam messages now". Finish on the Google storage page showing the used amount before and after. Use real numbers from a real account, not a promised "5GB".
research.notes: Verdict is ADJUST: the technique works, but the angle's numbers are not supportable. Rewrite the hook to something like "Before you pay for Google storage, run these 4 Gmail searches", and drop "5GB in 2 minutes". Use the four queries as: (1) has:attachment larger:10M, (2) category:promotions older_than:2y, (3) older_than:2y larger:10M, (4) has:attachment older_than:2y (the writer's 4th search). The final step is emptying Trash and Spam, because deleted mail still counts until then. The select-all banner is the step most people miss, so show it on screen. Two things I couldn't confirm from Google's own pages: exact current Gmail UI labels (Gmail help text says "Select" checkbox, "Delete" and "Empty Trash now"; older guides capitalise "Empty Trash Now") and the exact mobile-app label for Spam (some sources say "Empty Spam now"). Record a real session to get them right. The 15 GB vs 5 GB free-storage change (May 2026) is a timely hook: check your quota, and a phone number may unlock 15 GB for free. The Google One Basic price of $1.99/mo for 100 GB is US only, and prices differ by region (e.g. €1.99 in the EU). Source quality: the operator and Trash/Spam steps come from Google's own help pages; UI layout details come from third-party guides and my knowledge of Gmail's layout.
